summary: Session ghosting and silent unpin observed after version-lock switchover
description: Issue summary: During an operator-initiated version-lock switchover (canary -> primary), a subset of client sessions retained a stale session pointer ('ghost session') that appeared to remain pinned to the previous model for several minutes and then silently lost the pin mid-request. Impact: Customers reported mixed responses (stylistic mismatch and hallucinations) as part of single user sessions; several LLM calls returned tokens from two different model variants in one stream. Environment: Dedicated cluster (MapleAI), prod-us-east, reserved pool: d-prod-nyc-4g, traffic routed through dedicated-proxy. Observed behavior: Session affinity initially held to the pinned version for affected sessions, then mid-utterance the routing layer diverted to the canary fallback path without a logged pin eviction event. Expected behavior: Sessions pinned by customer version-lock should remain routed to pinned model instance until explicit unpin or session expiry. Affected customers noticed user-visible incoherence and flagged as P1.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer creates a version-lock on route /chat to redwood/fastgen-1.3 for session_cohort A; 2) Initiate canary switchover via Console: promote canary weight from 10% to 70% over 2 minutes; 3) Replay recorded user session traffic at production QPS for 3-5 minutes; 4) Observe responses where prefix tokens map to fastgen-1.3 but suffix tokens are consistent with vicuna-13b-ggml; 5) Check routing logs and session-store for pin metadata. Note: reproduction requires dedicated-proxy + proxy-side autoscale event during weight change to be most reliable.
observed_logs: [2026-03-10T15:02:12Z] routing: session_lookup id=ses_8f7a123 found pin=fastgen-1.3 ttl=900; [2026-03-10T15:02:14Z] proxy: shard-02 reported backend-change model=vicuna-13b-ggml reason=canary-weight-adjust; [2026-03-10T15:02:14Z] serving-runtime: request resumed kvcache=hit session=ses_8f7a123 route=/chat -> routed_backend=vicuna-13b-ggml; [2026-03-10T15:02:15Z] audit: no explicit pin-eviction event for ses_8f7a123; [2026-03-10T15:02:17Z] trace: token-stream shows token_1..token_36 from fastgen-1.3 then token_37..token_120 from vicuna-13b-ggml.
investigation_notes: - Initial hypothesis: race between dedicated-proxy shard failover and in-memory session-store leading to ephemeral loss of pin metadata under heavy prefix-preserving batching. - Confirmed that session-store uses local LRU cache with 30s heartbeat to central store; during proxy autoscale the local cache dropped entries before TTL refresh completed. - Found a path in routing code where on backend-change we call refresh_session_pin() but the call is best-effort and suppressed if proxy heartbeat is stale. That suppression path did not log an eviction event; this explains the 'silent unpin'. - Replayed traffic in staging with instrumentation: reproduced 18/200 runs (~9%) when autoscale event occurred within 250ms of a request completion. - Not correlated with auth tokens or customer pin APIs; appears purely routing+cache timing.
workaround: Short-term: advise customer to increase session_pin_ttl to 1800s and enable sticky-proxy=true for the route. If they expect rolling promotions, recommend scheduling promotions during low-traffic windows. Manual mitigation applied for MapleAI: temporarily pinned cohort to dedicated instance with static routing until hot path fix is deployed.
resolution: Partial fix deployed to staging (2026-03-13): routing now performs synchronous pin-refresh when backend-change is detected and logs an explicit eviction event when best-effort refresh is skipped. Full rollout to prod scheduled after canary verification. For MapleAI we coordinated a temporary routing rule to pin affected cohorts and will monitor. Follow-up patch to session-store heartbeat logic scheduled (PR referenced).
follow_up_actions: Roll out sync-pin-refresh to prod with 10% canary (owner: routing team)
Add an alert when session_pin_ttl-refresh failures > 0.5% over 5m
Update Console UI to surface sticky-proxy flag for dedicated routes
Postmortem & runbook update: document silent-unpin signature and mitigation steps
